- **HER COMPILER**: The record cross-references the RCAHMW Inventory Vol IV Part 2 and seven related events through 2013.
- **HER OFFICER**: This official record independently corroborates the demolition on 6 December 1988.
- Source: GGAT HER PRN 02038s — Compiled 21-08-1991; GGATE000877: Great House Farm Archaeological Assessment (1990)

### 1990 — GGAT Field Evaluation

In August 1990 GGAT digs eight machine trenches for BP. The eastern area 'could not be investigated', yet is zoned low potential. Early-medieval burials are found.

- **GGAT ARCHAEOLOGIST**: Eight trenches. The eastern area could not be investigated.
- **FAMILY RESEARCHER**: So how could it be called low potential?
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com)

### 1992 — Llandough

William (Billy) Buckler dies on 15 May 1992. Later that year reserved matters for 20 houses (92/00671/RES) are approved, 38 days after GGAT warns that significant deposits including human bone remain.

- **BRANWEN BUCKLER**: Billy fought for that house until the day he died.
- **PLANNING OFFICER**: Twenty houses approved.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com)

### 1993 — Former Farm Site

On 3 December 1993 BP transfers the site to Ideal Homes, and groundworks begin before the archaeological condition has been met.

- **SITE FOREMAN**: Groundworks start Monday.
- **GGAT ARCHAEOLOGIST**: Not before the archaeological condition is met.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com)

### 1994 — Cemetery Excavation, Former Farm Site

In 1994, after a Home Office licence (21 March) and agreement to 'preservation by record', the Cotswold Archaeological Trust excavates an early-medieval cemetery on the former farm site. Burials are found in the zone GGAT's 1990 evaluation had called low potential, many just below the topsoil. Published totals reach 1,026 burials, the largest early-medieval burial population then recovered from Wales.

> CHALLENGE: The site was developed into 20 houses, permanently erasing the physical evidence. No public inquiry was held into the demolition or the family's eviction.

- **LEAD ARCHAEOLOGIST**: This is an early-medieval cemetery, and a very large one.
- **WILLIAMS DESCENDANT**: And the 1990 report said this ground was low potential.
- **ARCHAEOLOGIST**: Many burials are only centimetres below the topsoil.
- **LEAD ARCHAEOLOGIST**: This is one of the largest burial grounds ever excavated in Wales.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com)

### 1994 — Woodland — WA735527

On 10 November 1994 the woodland, title WA735527, is transferred to Forest of Cardiff. The wiki places the woodland in Parcel A.

- **CONVEYANCER**: The woodland title passes to Forest of Cardiff.
- **FAMILY RESEARCHER**: That is the half of the land we are asking to have back.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki — Master Timeline (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/); Great House Farm Wiki — Woodland (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/)

### 1995–96 — HM Land Registry — WA231076 File

Rights are granted to South Wales Electricity, and there is correspondence with Persimmon. This is the last dealing on the registration file.

- **LAND REGISTRY CLERK**: The last entries on the file are the electricity rights and the Persimmon letters.
- **FAMILY RESEARCHER**: Then the paper trail on this title stops in the mid-1990s.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki — Master Timeline (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/); Great House Farm Wiki — Land Registry Titles (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings)

### 2005 — Heritage Website

The 1994 excavation is published (814 articulated burials). Heritage publications celebrate the Llandough archaeology but omit the eviction and demolition; residents live over the site unaware of the dispossession.

- **HERITAGE EDITOR**: We present the villa and burials as a heritage success, not an eviction site.
- **MODERN RESIDENT**: I learned of Roman remains here, not of a family being removed.
- **HERITAGE EDITOR**: The archaeology is the story we tell—the human cost is not our focus.
- **MODERN RESIDENT**: So the history is sanitized? The Bucklers erased from the site's narrative?
- **HERITAGE EDITOR**: Our remit is archaeological heritage, not contemporary property disputes.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com)

### 2005 — Woodland — WA735527

On 22 December 2005 part of the woodland title is divided off.

- **LAND REGISTRY CLERK**: Part of the woodland is split off into a separate title.
- **FAMILY RESEARCHER**: One more change to trace on the Parcel A land.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki — Master Timeline (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/); Great House Farm Wiki — Woodland (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/)

### 2019 — RCAHMW National Archive

On 20 March 2019 GGAT's 1990 assessment is accessioned to the national record, about 28 years after it was written.

- **ARCHIVIST**: The 1990 Great House Farm assessment, accessioned today.
- **FAMILY RESEARCHER**: Twenty-eight years later. Where was it all that time?
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com)

### 2025–26 — Public Bodies

The family make records requests to public bodies, logged step by step in the wiki's Records Access Chronology.

- **FAMILY RESEARCHER**: Every request, reply and refusal goes on the public record.
- **RECORDS OFFICER**: Your request has been received and will be dealt with under the Act.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki — Master Timeline (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/); Great House Farm Wiki — Records Access Chronology (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/)

### 2026 — Public Bodies

The family's records campaign. February–July: a complaint to HM Land Registry is refused at both stages, and a schedule of files is released. September: a letter to the MP, a complaint to Cadw about the 1988 listing decision, and a complaint and records requests to Heneb; the Great House Farm Wiki launches on 22 September. No court or public body has yet found in the family's favour on title.

- **FAMILY**: We are asking every public body for the records, one by one.
- **RECORDS OFFICER**: Your complaint has been logged and an investigating officer appointed.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com); greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/

### 2026 — Great House Farm Wiki — Press Archive

On 3 October 2026 fifteen newspaper cuttings from the family archive, Google Drive and email are transcribed onto the wiki, from the 1891 court report to the 1989 coverage.

- **ARCHIVIST**: Fifteen cuttings transcribed, each with its date and paper.
- **FAMILY RESEARCHER**: Now the press record can be checked by anyone.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki — Master Timeline (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/); Great House Farm Wiki — Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/)

### Present Day — Church View Close

Church View Close now covers the site of Great House Farm, the Marconi base, and one of Wales's largest recorded burial excavations, yet no plaque or record notes the clearance or dispute.

- **RESIDENT'S CHILD**: Dad, I want to build a radio and plant a tree and own this house we live in.
- **FATHER**: Don't think that way or say that out loud, son. It brings us big trouble here.
- **RESIDENT'S CHILD**: But why?
- **FATHER**: The last family to speak like that are traumatised into silence, three decades later.
- **RESIDENT'S CHILD**: Well, I will speak up. And for them too.

### Present Day — Legal Archive

What the records establish: the family lost BP Properties Ltd v Buckler; Cadw decided not to list; BP demolished the house on 6 December 1988; the Royal Commission's recording was left incomplete; several key records are missing. What the family contend: the farm was two parcels, the house parcel never passed to WGR and BP, and documents about it were never before the courts.

- **LEGAL RESEARCHER**: Every court avoided the ownership question—the only issue that mattered.
- **HISTORIAN**: The 1667 deed, manorial records, Mary Williams' journal—all missing or destroyed.
- **LEGAL RESEARCHER**: The Roman burial was reported in 1870 but ignored until post-demolition excavation.
- **HISTORIAN**: Mary Williams became Mrs Buckler in legal documents without explanation or consent.
- **LEGAL RESEARCHER**: Under Takhar v Gracefield, fraud unravels all—but only if investigated.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com)

### Present Day — Academic Conference

Legal scholars note the case exemplifies how procedural avoidance, missing documentation, and rushed demolition can circumvent substantive justice and heritage protection.

- **LAW PROFESSOR**: This case shows how possession can be determined without addressing ownership.
- **HERITAGE EXPERT**: Demolition before listing creates irreversible loss of heritage and evidence.
- **LAW PROFESSOR**: The Williams-Buckler family asserted ownership for 321 years without force or secrecy.
- **HERITAGE EXPERT**: While corporate claimants operated through licence, substitution, and stealth.
- **LAW PROFESSOR**: Justice requires investigation: who owned it? Where are the deeds? Why the rush?

### Present Day — Public Inquiry Call

Advocates call for a public inquiry to examine the combined effect of procedural avoidance, identity substitution, heritage omission, and irreversible consequence in the Great House Farm case.

> CHALLENGE: The family allege fraud, concealment and unlawful demolition, and estimate reparations above £100 million. No court or public body has made such a finding, and no inquiry has been held.

- **ADVOCATE**: No public inquiry has examined how this dispossession was achieved.
- **PARLIAMENTARIAN**: What remedy exists when courts avoid ownership and demolition destroys evidence?
- **ADVOCATE**: Declaratory justice: determine who owned it, correct the record, recognise the Williams-Buckler claim. The 2026 Wales Reparation Case stands as a test of whether the legal system can correct centuries of injustice.
- **PARLIAMENTARIAN**: And if fraud is established, what compensation is owed?
- **ADVOCATE**: Preliminarily quantified at approximately £101.2 million, but truth comes first.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com)
